constructor:rack::ui::PasswordField::Pas.finding: P1: PasswordField() only sets password = true (include/ui/TextField.hpp, PasswordField ctor), but the cited test asserts only isinstance(ui.PasswordField(), ui.TextField) (tests/ui/in_rack/test_widgets.py:254). field:rack::ui::TextField::text.finding: P2: cursor and selection are clamped because 'Rack indexes the text with them' (native/bindings/ui/ui.cpp:258-267; docs/reference/ui.md text-fields). The raw text setter (ui.cpp:249-251) does not re-clamp them, though. Assigning a shorter text leaves cursor/selection past the end, which Rack's TextField::onSelectKey asserts against (src/ui/TextField.cpp: assert(cursor <= (int) text.size())), and which makes insert_text/get_selected_text raise. Smallest fix: clamp cursor/selection after a text write, or document that a raw text write can leave them out of range.

field:rack::widget::SvgWidget::svg.finding: P2: the setter refuses an Svg with no parsed image (ValueError via drawableSvg, native/bindings/widget/managed.hpp:157-161, used at variants_svg.cpp:53). The restriction is justified (Rack's svgDraw dereferences svg->handle unchecked), but the cited anchor docs/reference/widgets.md#typed-bases (187-191) does not document it. Smallest fix: add 'None or a loaded Svg; an unloaded Svg raises ValueError' to typed-bases.

function:rack::ui::refreshTheme().finding: P1: tests/ui/in_rack/test_widgets.py:450-470 calls ui.refresh_theme() and only checks RackPy's off-main-thread ThreadError. Nothing observes that Rack's theme was restored, so a no-op binding would pass. Smallest fix: set_theme to distinctive colours, render a widget, call refresh_theme, re-render, and assert the pixels change back (framebuffer read-back as in tests/rendering).

function:rack::ui::setTheme(NVGcolor, NV.finding: P1: tests/ui/in_rack/test_widgets.py:451 calls ui.set_theme(...) with no assertion, so a no-op binding would pass. Smallest fix: render a Button/TextField in a FramebufferWidget before and after set_theme(bg, fg) and assert the read-back colour changes.

macro:RIGHT_ARROW.finding: P2: docs/reference/ui.md#ui-theme (162-163) says everything there needs Rack's main thread, but RIGHT_ARROW is a plain module str (native/bindings/ui/ui.cpp:379) with record thread 'any'. Smallest fix: exempt the macros in that sentence.

method:rack::ui::Slider::draw(const rack.finding: P1: no cited test checks Slider::draw. The only drawing test, tests/ui/in_rack/test_widgets.py:208-229 (test_rack_draws_the_widgets), calls frame.render() twice and asserts nothing. Python Slider.draw(args) is never called, so a wrong or no-op binding would still pass. Smallest fix: render a Slider with a quantity into a FramebufferWidget, read back its pixels (as tests/rendering/in_rack/test_rendering.py does), or assert a Python draw override calling super().draw(args) produces bndSlider output.

method:rack::ui::Slider::onDragEnd(const.finding: P1: no cited test calls Slider.on_drag_end. tests/ui/in_rack/test_widgets.py:96-120 calls on_drag_start/on_drag_end on the Button only, and test_slider_double_click_resets_quantity (157-168) covers only on_double_click and on_drag_move. Smallest fix: call slider.on_drag_start / on_drag_end with button=0 and assert Rack's cursor-lock state, or at least that the quantity is unchanged and no error is logged.

method:rack::ui::Slider::onDragStart(con.finding: P1: no cited test calls Slider.on_drag_start. tests/ui/in_rack/test_widgets.py:108 calls it on a ui.Button, not the Slider, so Rack's Slider::onDragStart (src/ui/Slider.cpp: button check, then cursorLock) is never run. Smallest fix: add slider.on_drag_start(w.DragStartEvent(button=0)) with an assertion (cursor-lock state, or that a non-left button is ignored).

method:rack::ui::TextField::copyClipboar.finding: P1: the cited test cannot tell whether copy_clipboard works. tests/ui/in_rack/test_widgets.py:268-272 calls copy_clipboard() and then cut_clipboard(), which copies again (Rack's cutClipboard calls copyClipboard), before paste_clipboard() is asserted. method:rack::ui::TextField::onButton(con.finding: P1: no cited test calls TextField.on_button. method:rack::ui::Tooltip::step().finding: P1: no test calls Tooltip.step() or steps a Tooltip. The cited test_fields_round_trip (test_widgets.py:38-65) only sets and reads text. method:rack::widget::FramebufferWidget::.finding: P1: no cited test runs FramebufferWidget::draw. The cited tests use frame.render() (render -> drawFramebuffer -> children), e.g. tests/widget/in_rack/test_drawing.py:66,91,114 and test_variants.py:265, and never call frame.draw(args) or let Rack draw the frame itself. tests/rendering/test_frames.py does run it (clean/dirty re-render counts and the composited framebuffer pixel) but is not cited for this record. Smallest fix: cite tests/rendering/test_frames.py::test_framebuffers_and_the_self_lit_layer_in_real_frames.

P2: the behaviour is tested (test_variants.py:263-266), but the only cited anchor, docs/reference/widgets.md#typed-bases (193-195), does not mention get_image_handle. It is described under #drawing (widgets.md:163-164), which this record does not cite. Smallest fix: add docs/reference/widgets.md#drawing to docs.

P1: the test cannot tell whether on_context_create runs Rack's implementation. In test_scene.py:110-151 the override calls super().on_context_create(), and the test asserts bool(frame.dirty). But RackPy's own graphics-context-create hook marks every managed framebuffer dirty anyway (native/bindings/widget/managed.cpp:185-190), and the detached frame passes the same assertion. The test_events cases cover only Widget.on_context_create. Smallest fix: on a rendered detached frame with set_dirty(False), call frame.on_context_create(w.ContextCreateEvent(...)) directly and assert dirty becomes True and a child override receives the event.

P1: Rack's FramebufferWidget::onContextDestroy is never run by a cited test. The test_scene.py:113-116 override deliberately skips super(), and RackPy's hook frees the framebuffer instead (managed.cpp:174-183). The test_events cases call only Widget.on_context_destroy. Smallest fix: render a detached frame, call frame.on_context_destroy(w.ContextDestroyEvent(...)), and assert get_framebuffer() is None, get_image_handle() == -1 and dirty is True.

P2: the behaviour is tested (test_variants.py:259-260), but the only cited anchor, docs/reference/widgets.md#typed-bases (193-195), lists the dirty field and not set_dirty(), or its default of True. Smallest fix: mention set_dirty(dirty=True) in typed-bases, or cite an anchor that describes it.

P1: the only test calling FramebufferWidget.step is tests/widget/in_rack/test_variants.py:29-49. It checks that Rack calls the Python override (calls == [1]) on a frame with no children. Nothing checks what base.step(self) does (Rack's FramebufferWidget::step is Widget::step, which steps the children), so a no-op binding would pass. Smallest fix: give the frame a child whose step override records the call, then call FramebufferWidget.step(frame) and assert the child stepped.

method:rack::widget::OpenGlWidget::drawF.finding: P1: no cited test runs OpenGlWidget::drawFramebuffer. test_drawing.py:99-121 subclasses w.FramebufferWidget, not OpenGlWidget, and test_variants.py:29-49 only steps an OpenGlWidget child. Rack's OpenGlWidget::drawFramebuffer (src/widget/OpenGlWidget.cpp:16-35: clear plus RGB triangle) is never run. Smallest fix: render() an OpenGlWidget, or call its draw_framebuffer from an override, and assert e.g. a red corner pixel in the framebuffer read-back.

method:rack::widget::OpenGlWidget::step(.finding: P1: Rack's OpenGlWidget::step sets dirty = true every frame (src/widget/OpenGlWidget.cpp:9-13). The only cited test, test_variants.py:29-49, asserts just that the Python override was called. Smallest fix: set_dirty(False), call OpenGlWidget.step(gl), and assert gl.dirty is True.

method:rack::widget::TransformWidget::dr.finding: P1: no cited test draws a TransformWidget. TransformWidget appears only in test_variants.py:29-49 (step round trip) and 123-180 (matrix math). P1: no cited test runs TransformWidget::drawLayer. TransformWidget is used only in test_variants.py:29-49 and 123-180, and test_drawing.py's draw_layer test uses plain Widgets.
